title: Experimental coupled GPU cells: material/contact/body motion audited; realtime remains open
changes: New /coupled 3D page: nine connected finite cells, density-derived ball, fixed supports, actual CUDA material/contact/body solve, Before/Live and downloadable complete microstep records. Low-energy four-material controls pass; fracture/yield and realtime remain unqualified.

GPU material inspector now shows actual CUDA force directions and body force/torque pairs. General finite-frame reactions use the same CPU/CUDA energy gradient; normal controlled loading has zero torque. The diagram still has no dynamics clock.

GPU material laws at /materials runs persistent damage and six-mode plastic return from shared C++ source via CuPy. Apply a common opening, unload and inspect retained history. Controlled constitutive loading only, not dynamic GPU fracture or dents.

PhysX reuses resident CUDA pose/velocity buffers. Every substep is retained; all 15360 refined stack states match the independent column reference exactly. The slower column path remains available in the profiler.
GPU lab shows actual SDK stepping, GPU observation and host audit time. Every calculated substep remains recorded; constitutive port is separate from this rigid solver.
GPU solver now compares Newton XPBD and PhysX TGS in the same 3D world. Stack control uses zero bounce/friction and 1/1920 s; glass/oak/iron/ice complete in scoped controls.
PhysX records actual CUDA poses, mass/inertia and normal contact impulses each substep. Friction and full contact/numerical work are not yet in that account; no bonded GPU fracture or dents.
Open GPU contact yard: CUDA-calculated ball drops, two-body impacts and free fall. CPU material lab remains available; no GPU fracture or dents yet.
GPU frames use actual resident Newton/Warp states, with every substep recorded. The full 27-block stack stops at an energy refusal and retains its last accepted scene.
Optional Contact response → Coupled friction + bounce solves sliding and twist together while retaining native material restitution. Reference stays default.
Physics step selects the actual 1/960 or refined 1/1920 s experiment. Before/Live shows original and accepted native geometry.

The reproduced refined glass refusal is twisting friction adding energy in the direction of existing spin. Terminal rejected records now retain original-cell impulses and actual force/solver velocities.
Glass/oak/iron/ice complete at both timesteps in the initial trial. Full convergence, large energy deficits, connected calculation speed and thermal/fluid/power laws remain unfinished.
